publications.headline: Data Breaches & Exploited Vulnerabilities Dominate Cybersecurity News

articles.headline: Gîtes de France Breach Data Added to Have I Been Pwned
articles.summary: Data from a May 2026 breach at the French holiday rental network Gîtes de France has been added to the Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) notification service. The incident, attributed to the hacker 'ChimeraZ,' exposed the personal and booking details of hundreds of thousands of customers. The indexed dataset includes 117,574 unique email addresses, along with names, phone numbers, and physical addresses, putting affected individuals at high risk of targeted phishing scams.

articles.headline: Microsoft Remains Top Impersonated Brand in Q3 2026 Phishing Attacks
articles.summary: According to a Q3 2026 report from Check Point Research, Microsoft continues to be the most impersonated brand in phishing attacks, accounting for 33% of all such attempts. This is a significant jump from the previous quarter and far exceeds other commonly spoofed brands like Apple and Google. The report also highlights a new trend of attackers impersonating AI and developer platforms, such as Anthropic's Claude and Google's Antigravity, to steal credentials, payment details, and achieve remote code execution.

articles.headline: Burger King Japan App Breach Exposes 11.18 Million Customer Records
articles.summary: Burger King Japan has disclosed a major data breach affecting approximately 11.18 million members of its official smartphone app. Unauthorized access to a customer membership system between October 2 and October 7, 2026, resulted in the exposure of extensive personally identifiable information (PII), including names, phone numbers, dates of birth, and addresses. While the company states that credit card data and passwords were not compromised, the leaked PII places millions of customers at high risk of targeted phishing and identity theft.

articles.headline: Helix Ransomware Group Claims Attack on American Campus
articles.summary: The Helix ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on American Campus, a major US-based student housing provider with an estimated annual revenue of $1 billion. The group posted the claim on its dark web leak site on October 19, 2026, threatening to release exfiltrated data within hours. This attack is part of a recent wave of high-profile targets claimed by the Helix group, employing a double extortion strategy.

articles.headline: OpenCode Breach Exposes OpenAI, Anthropic API Keys, Leads to Fraud
articles.summary: The open-source AI coding agent OpenCode has disclosed a security breach that exposed user API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The incident, which affected 1.4% of its Console users, resulted from unauthorized access to a legacy system. Attackers used the stolen keys in a 'distillation attack,' running up significant fraudulent charges on user accounts to likely train their own AI models. OpenCode has notified affected users and advised them to revoke and replace the compromised keys.

articles.headline: CISA Warns of Actively Exploited BeyondTrust Flaw Used by Chinese APT
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The flaw, which allows for arbitrary file operations, has been actively exploited as a zero-day since August 2026 by a suspected China-linked espionage group, ARMORY CASTLE. The attackers use the flaw to gain initial access, escalate privileges, and deploy custom malware. BeyondTrust has released patches, and CISA urges all organizations to update immediately.

articles.headline: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack on M365
articles.summary: ConnectWise has suspended its Cloud Backup services following a sophisticated supply chain attack. Threat actors compromised an application credential, gaining unauthorized access to the Microsoft 365 tenants of numerous Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and their customers. The attack, which bypasses user-level MFA, allowed for broad data access and privilege escalation. ConnectWise has disabled the affected application identities and is investigating the incident, which Microsoft has classified as an active supply chain attack.

articles.headline: Millions of California Student Records Exposed in Breach at Vendor ETS
articles.summary: A massive data breach at Educational Testing Service (ETS), a contractor for the California Department of Education (CDE), has exposed the personal data of millions of current and former California public school students. An attacker used a compromised SFTP login credential to access and copy sensitive files for nearly four months, from May to September 2026. The exposed data includes names, dates of birth, home addresses, student identifiers, and disability status. ETS is offering identity protection services to all affected individuals.

articles.headline: Health Network and IT Firm to Pay $2.7M for Breach of 888,000 Patient Records
articles.summary: Boston Children's Health Physicians (BCHP) and its IT service provider, XTIUM, have agreed to a $2.7 million settlement with the attorneys general of New York and Connecticut. The settlement resolves investigations into a 2024 data breach originating at XTIUM that exposed the sensitive personal and medical data of nearly 888,000 pediatric patients. The compromised information included Social Security numbers, medical details, and financial records. The companies are also required to implement stronger data security measures.

articles.headline: High-Severity SQL Injection Flaw in Modern Events Calendar WordPress Plugin
articles.summary: A high-severity SQL injection vulnerability, CVE-2026-96534, has been disclosed in the popular Modern Events Calendar Lite and Pro WordPress plugins. The flaw, rated 7.7 on the CVSS scale, allows an authenticated attacker with low-level permissions, such as a Subscriber, to execute malicious SQL queries. A successful exploit could lead to the exfiltration of sensitive information from the website's database. All versions prior to 7.37.0 are affected, and administrators are urged to update immediately.

articles.headline: Millions of California Students' Data Exposed in Breach at Testing Provider
articles.summary: A massive data breach at Educational Testing Service (ETS), a contractor for California's public school system, has compromised the personal information of millions of current and former students. The breach, which occurred between May and September 2026, exposed names, birth dates, addresses, and sensitive disability information. The attackers gained access using a compromised login credential for a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site. State officials confirmed that Social Security numbers were not exposed, and ETS is offering identity protection services to all affected individuals.

articles.headline: Plex Media Server Exploit Chain Deploys Cryptomining Malware in the Wild
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a chain of four vulnerabilities in unpatched Plex Media Server software to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). The exploit, publicly available as 'Plex2Shell', is being used to install cryptocurrency mining malware on compromised servers. The flaws affect versions prior to 1.43.3.10828, and users, especially those on NAS devices, are urged to update immediately. Honeypot activity confirmed active scanning and exploitation from multiple IP addresses.

articles.headline: Report: 40% of Ransomware Attacks Now Involve Physical Threats to Staff
articles.summary: A new report from Semperis reveals a disturbing escalation in ransomware tactics, with 40% of attacks now involving psychological or physical threats against employees and their families. This 'triple extortion' method, which includes sending intimidating packages and threatening physical harm, is designed to pressure companies into paying ransoms even if they have viable data backups. The report also found that 84% of ransomware attacks now leverage artificial intelligence, increasing the sophistication of campaigns.

articles.headline: Chinese APT 'Armory Castle' Exploited BeyondTrust Zero-Day for Espionage
articles.summary: A suspected Chinese state-sponsored threat actor, tracked as Armory Castle (UNC5221), has been actively exploiting a critical zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances since at least August 2026. The flaw, CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS 9.8), allows for full system compromise, enabling the attackers to steal credentials and deploy custom malware for long-term espionage. CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating immediate action from federal agencies.

articles.headline: Compromised ConnectWise Credential Used to Breach 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
articles.summary: A single compromised ConnectWise service account with delegated admin privileges (DAP) was leveraged by attackers to gain unauthorized access to the Microsoft 365 environments of 173 organizations. The attack, which began on October 13, 2026, allowed threat actors to access sensitive data in mailboxes, OneDrive, and SharePoint. In response, ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup service and disabled multiple application identities to prevent further unauthorized authentication. The incident highlights the significant risks associated with broad permissions in managed service provider (MSP) supply chains.

articles.headline: Hundreds of French Supermarket Refrigeration Controllers Exposed Online After Hack
articles.summary: Days after a cyberattack caused widespread disruption by remotely heating refrigeration units in hundreds of French supermarkets, security researchers report that hundreds of these industrial control systems (ICS) remain exposed to the internet. The attack, which is under investigation, targeted controllers from Danfoss and Copeland, causing food spoilage and even fires. The continued exposure highlights critical vulnerabilities in operational technology (OT) security within the retail sector.
